differences.what: roof: the engraving's mansard, its steep lower faces bowed a little to a curb about 2.9 m over the cornice, under a low upper hip; the build's was a 30-degree tin hip
wall head: the engraving's cornice stands about 8.2 m over grade (its soffit 7.9 m); the build's walls stood 0.7 m higher

north pavilion: the north 3.75 m of the front (v 7.5-11.25) is a pavilion standing a little proud, with two round-headed windows a storey under moulded hoods and a light corner strip at its north corner; the build's front is flat there and carries the canted bay
crown: over the pavilion a taller bell-curved mansard with one round-headed dormer, rising about 0.7 m over the main curb; the build has none
corner strip: the engraving draws a light strip down the pavilion's north corner, a stone or painted quoin; T-2404's pavilion turns that corner in its own brick

dormers: round-headed dormers in the mansard's lower face, two seen on the north face, their arch heads at x 746 and 805 px (51 and 110 px behind the crown's front-north corner) reaching about 10.5 m, just under the curb; built so by T-2411, two K06 round-arched sash in stone faces at u 12.6 and 6.1 m, landing at x 756 and 813 px, 47 and 106 px behind the build's crown corner (which itself stands about 10 px right of the engraving's). The engraver draws both wider and more frontal than the camera allows; the front's lower slope is behind the trees

bay window: a one-storey canted bay on the SOUTH part of the front, its front's edges at x 437 and 488 px and its north cheek's foot at 512 px (v 1.54-4.64, 0.58 m out), two round-headed lights in its front, under a flared hood on a console at each corner of its front with a row of modillions; built so by T-2408 (k08.bay.canted_hooded), its edges landing at x 440 and 492 px. The picture's finial is the foot of the upper window that stands on the hood's top, and is not a finial

windows: round-headed sash under moulded hoods on the street front, the upper window over the bay and the one over the door each with an ornate crown over its hood; the north wall's windows flat-headed, two a storey, at x 737 and 810 px (3.35 and 11.55 m back from the front corner). Built so by T-2410: both upper street windows K06's round-headed fanlight sash in a round hole through the brick under the kit's stone arch band, a key block on each crown for the ornament the engraving draws but does not resolve; the north wall's three windows a storey are now the engraving's two, flat-headed

the upper window over the door: the engraving draws it at x 530-550 px, about v 5.6-6.1; the build stands it on the door's own centre, which T-2409 moved to v 6.6, so it stands about 0.5-1 m north of the drawn one (the K01 bay puts the door and the window over it on one centre)

entrance: the door beside the pavilion's south face under a hood, reached by a straight stoop whose north string is the rail rising to the right from x 540 to 582 px (on this camera a line running back toward the wall draws so; one running north along the front would rise over about 80 px, not 42), at its head a porch at the principal floor running north before the pavilion to the north corner behind a turned balustrade that carries on down the stoop. Built (T-2409): the door at v 6.6 under a K09 cornice hood on consoles, the straight stoop's north string at v 7.65 (drawn at x 572 to 541 px), a stone terrace 1.2 m deep before the pavilion to the corner (its north end at x 685.6 px against the engraving's 690) behind a turned balustrade carried down both cheeks. The engraving draws this front's floor, porch and fence about 1.5-2 m lower against the house than this camera's grade puts them (the porch's rail top at about 0.25 m, the bay's sills at about 0.4 m); the same offset stands under the bay, so it is the camera's height datum, filed on T-2406, not the entrance

fence: a lattice of interlaced pointed arches on a solid base along the street line, a board fence on the north side; the build's is the K11 scroll-band iron fence on a stone curb with stone gate piers and urns
chimney: a tall stack at the front of the north wall, rising from the cornice beside the crown; the build's two stacks stand on the ridge
roof covering: the lower faces read as slate in courses; the build's is painted standing-seam tin (K04 slates nothing under 25 degrees, and the upper hip is 18)

bay window's heights: the engraving draws the bay's sills about 0.4 m over grade and its eaves level with the pavilion's lower window heads, about 0.75 m lower than the build's, on the low principal floor it draws everywhere; the build stands the bay on the house's reconstructed 1.4 m principal floor
bay window's tone: the engraving draws the bay dark against the light front (the hood's shadow, or a painted timber bay); built in the house's brick
bay window's terrace: a low balustrade runs before the bay at its foot; the build has none (T-2409's porch)

walls' tone: the engraving draws the front light and the north wall and the pavilion's north half dark, its light from the south-east; the house's colour (the Inter Ocean's 'olive green' of 1887) and its walling are not shown in a monochrome print
the south side wall and the rear: the engraving sees neither
